summary.statement: Only vendor estimates exist: Rs18-35 per flagged order (Rs90k-1.75 lakh/month at 5,000 orders) from Shipway; Rs10-50 per flagged shipment from Eshopbox; 2-5% of freight at 10,000+ parcels from Prozo.

A worked example from a reconciliation vendor puts permanent weight leakage at ~Rs84,000 on Rs58 lakh monthly spend (~1.4%), and COD exceptions at 0.4-1.2% of COD value, suggesting recoverable amounts for a 300-5,000 parcel seller may be small.
Individual sellers report charges of Rs100-150 per extra kg and losing whole made-to-order products to fake RTOs, but no seller-stated monthly total was found.
Disputes require 4-5 photos of the parcel on a scale with tape measurements; sellers who pre-upload such images still report losing disputes.
Couriers and aggregators advise photographing shipments as proof; Shiprocket's freeze needs 5 package images per SKU.
No source documents a warehouse SOP from a D2C brand of the ICP size.
Estimates of flagged shipments range from 4-9% of AWBs to 5-20%; one seller reports 90% of orders flagged.
Windows are short (7 working days on Shiprocket, 10 days on Velocity, 3-7 days typical) and missed ones auto-accept; Shiprocket's billing timeline averages 21 days.
Contest success: one vendor example assumes 40% of flagged AWBs won with evidence; seller complaints say disputes were rejected despite proof. No aggregator publishes a success rate.
Packing-video capture is already mandatory for Flipkart SPF eligibility and many cheap AWB-scan-triggered tools exist, so packers do adopt capture when a platform requires it.
An aggregator advises photographing only risky parcels, not every parcel, as per-parcel capture is impractical.
No evidence on the ~3-second step limit for packers.
COD remittance is reconciled by matching Shopify order exports to courier remittance files, usually in spreadsheets or not at all; estimates range from 30 min/week to 3-5 working days/month.
Companies staff this work with accounts executives, and dedicated tools (Cointab, BUSY Recom) exist.
Shiprocket exposes a public API including wallet/statements and discrepancy details (JWT, 10-day token), so reading data need not depend on scraping.
Disputes themselves are only accepted through the panel, once per order, so filing on a seller's behalf may still need panel access.
No Indian seller evidence on paying a subscription plus a share of recoveries. Analogues: Amazon FBA recovery services charge ~25% contingency (US), and packing-video tools sell from $15-30/month.

new_unknowns.question: What dispute success rate do ICP sellers actually get on Shiprocket/Delhivery/Xpressbees, and how much is lost to auto-accepts per month?
Will aggregators' own auto-dispute and weight-freeze features (Velocity, Shiprocket, iCarry) leave enough unrecovered money for a third-party overlay?

current_solutions.statement: Sellers dispute inside the aggregator's own panel with 4-5 scale/tape photos within a 7-day window; unanswered discrepancies auto-accept.
Aggregators and fulfilment providers increasingly auto-dispute or pre-freeze weights themselves (Shiprocket Weight Freeze, Velocity, Eshopbox, iCarry).
COD remittance is reconciled manually in spreadsheets or by gut feel; dedicated tools (Cointab, BUSY Recom) and aggregator dashboards exist.
Packing proof is captured with order/AWB-linked video tools, which Flipkart already mandates for seller protection.
